response: {"text":"The collection brings together sixteen research reports produced over two decades, most of which rely on statistical analysis and extensive data tables. The papers examine a range of psychiatric conditions and their connections to self‑harm, criminal behavior, and the likelihood of developing a disorder. Economic consequences of these illnesses are quantified, and long‑term patterns of a progressive neurodegenerative disease are traced. Several studies explore how genetic inheritance and environmental circumstances contribute to mood disorders and early‑onset psychotic illnesses. Two investigations focus on the role of a widely used intoxicant: one looks at its impact before, during, and after a period of legal restriction, while the other reviews three decades of cases in a large northeastern jurisdiction. The work offers detailed commentary and thoughtful interpretation for anyone studying mental health issues."}
